rv.q: The evening succeeds because it abounds with infectious, unfaked delight.

Nonetheless, Nikolai Foster’s production is brightly entertaining and blasts out room-filling energy in its big dance numbers by choreographer Arlene Phillips, with tight formations of sharp, rhythmic 50s motifs.
Though the humour in this production – with the exception of the loveably loud Mary Moore as Jan – could be cranked up a notch or two, this is a good night out.
All of this Nikolai Foster’s revival serves up with skill.
It’s a problem that this production doesn’t completely solve.

Alas, the more-or-less original narrative meanders purposelessly among a dectet of caterwauling Pink Ladies and gurning Burger Palace Boys (they only became T-Birds in the movie), stuttering from couple to couple, from sleepover to nonexistent street-fight.
Ultimately, this is a thunderously good evening out.
It succeeds on its own terms and we can't ask for much more than that.
But then that’s the core issue with this production, which feels caught between sombre realism and full-throttle, sugar-rush escapism.
If your tastes aren’t especially demanding (and you can forgive a bit of youthful inexperience), you’ll have a blast.
But as it is, this slow and dull production of Grease is very much not The One That I Want.
Fantastic staging and a truly brilliant cast make this production incredibly satisfying to watch and pure unashamed theatre joy.
Grease The Musical is a safe bet for audiences looking for a truly feel-good show in the summer nights ahead.
If director Nikolai Foster isn't the man for subtlety or dramaturgy, he and choreographer Arlene Phillips do lay on knock out set pieces, courtesy of their untried but energetic cast.
The result is a mixed bag of tricks.
Yet elsewhere there is very little about this show to like.
Nikolai Foster’s Leicester Curve production of Grease is awful mostly because it conforms to every expectation.

cn.t: This grittier take on the original stage musical divides critics, with some praising its energy and familiar songs while others find it lacklustre and charmless compared to the beloved film version.

vr.q: On balance there are also too many areas where I find the narrative gets a little bit confused and the characters aren't necessarily honored completely and so overall this is a three-star review from me.
